page: Microsoft Azure D32ps_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by 64-bit ARM architecture. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance is equipped with Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processors operating at 3.4 GHz. It delivers 32 dedicated physical cores with a one-to-one thread-to-core mapping, 128 MB of L3 cache, and 128.0 GB of memory. This configuration establishes a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The server includes AES cryptographic hardware acceleration but provides no bundled local ephemeral storage or discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark analysis highlights top-tier memory bandwidth and strong multi-core processing capabilities. The platform achieves 450.97 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 188.48 GB/sec in large-block write operations, placing its uncached memory subsystem in the top tier of evaluated cloud hardware. Multi-threaded benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core tests, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, and Clang compilation tasks, demonstrate strong performance scaling across all 32 physical cores. Conversely, single-core processing across Geekbench and stress-ng scores within average ranges, and large language model inference for 70B parameter models shows latency constraints.

Given the dedicated physical core layout and high memory throughput, the instance provides efficient scaling for parallelized compute tasks that rely on external persistent disks. D32ps_v6 is well suited for relational and in-memory database engines, multi-threaded Clang or C++ build pipelines, static web serving fleets, and general-purpose enterprise applications.
description: The Microsoft Azure D32ps_v6 is an ARM-based general-purpose virtual machine featuring Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processors running at 3.4 GHz. It provides 32 dedicated physical cores with single-threaded execution, 128 MB of L3 cache, and 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM allocation. The server contains no local storage volumes or GPU accelerators, depending on remote storage services for persistent data. Benchmark metrics reflect top-tier uncached memory bandwidth, reaching 450.97 GB/sec read and 188.48 GB/sec write speeds, coupled with top-tier database operation scores. Multi-core performance is strong across software compilation and compression workloads, whereas single-core performance remains average. D32ps_v6 offers resource efficiency for multi-threaded workloads, including database servers, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and high-concurrency web applications.
